questions.q: What is a Personal Legend in the story?
a: The unique dream or calling you are meant to pursue
A treasure map passed down through families
A prophecy given by the gypsy woman
The trade you inherit from your parents
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Melchizedek uses the phrase for the boy's calling.

questions.q: Why does the crystal merchant remain where he is?
a: He knows his dream but is too afraid to pursue it
He has already achieved his Personal Legend
He doubts the boy's omens
He cannot afford the journey to Egypt
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts his fear with the boy's decision to keep going.

questions.q: What happens once you commit to your dream, per the summary?
a: The universe helps, though difficulties still come
Obstacles vanish and the path turns easy
You no longer need teachers or mentors
Your fear disappears completely and permanently
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the universe conspires, but not without problems.

questions.q: Where is Santiago's treasure finally found?
a: Back in Spain, under the tree from his first dream
Beneath the pyramids in Egypt
In the oasis of Al-Fayoum
In the crystal merchant's shop
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a robber's dream reveals the true location.

questions.q: What is the summary's message about falling?
a: Getting up more often than you fall means you never fail
A single fall can undo years of progress
You should avoid any risk that could make you fall
Only talented people recover from failure quickly
questions.why: Lesson 3 quotes the idea of falling seven times and rising eight.
